narrative.overview:
This is an engineering console, not a consumer app — the references that actually landed in the build are QGIS/Mapbox Studio-style map-first layout, Grafana/Datadog-style dense monospace stat tiles, and Palantir Foundry's flat dark operational chrome. Every screen exists to show one comparison — OR-Tools (classical) against QPSO (quantum-inspired) — never one algorithm's output alone. The palette is functional, not decorative: two colors carry algorithm identity, one color carries eco-positive figures, and everything else is neutral lightness-stepped gray. There is exactly one theme; light mode was never built and is out of scope.

Confirmed rejections, carried from the brief and honored by the shipped code: no purple/violet gradients, no glowing particle/neural-net/"quantum swirl" motifs, no rounded bubbly consumer-SaaS cards, no illustrated/cartoon empty states, no decorative rainbow color use, no Unicode/emoji glyphs standing in for icons.
keyCharacteristics: Flat dark chrome, depth by lightness step (canvas -> surface -> surface-raised), never by shadow, except modals.
Inter for UI text, IBM Plex Mono for every measured number.
A colored left border is the app's one color-encoding mechanism, reused identically on every stat/status tile.
Two colors are reserved: they mean one thing each, everywhere, and nothing else.

rules.name: The One Meaning Rule
rules.body: route-classical, route-quantum, and accent-eco each mean exactly one thing and are never reused as a generic UI accent, hover color, or decorative highlight. This was the system's one material defect caught in finish review and the fix is now the rule.

rules.name: The Border-Encodes Rule
rules.body: Color-coding a tile is done with a 3px solid left border on an otherwise neutral card, never by tinting background or text.

rules.name: The Measured-Number Rule
rules.body: Any value read off a solver, sensor, or computation renders in font-mono; Inter is reserved for prose and labels.

rules.name: The Sticky-CTA Rule
rules.body: A screen's one primary action button sits in a position:sticky, bottom:0 footer so it stays reachable without scroll.

rules.name: The Flat-Except-Interrupt Rule
rules.body: Shadows exist only where content interrupts the console (the modal). Every persistent surface stays flat.

dos: Do render every measured number in font-mono, never in Inter.
Do encode algorithm or eco-figure identity with a 3px solid colored left border on an otherwise neutral card.
Do pair route-quantum with a dashed stroke and route-classical with a solid stroke everywhere a route/line appears.
Do pad a small/near-flat data series' Y-axis domain so a real-but-flat convergence line stays visibly drawn above the axis.
Do keep a screen's one primary CTA in a position:sticky, bottom:0 footer.
Do draw every icon as an inline SVG at one consistent stroke weight, never a Unicode/emoji glyph.
donts: Don't reuse route-classical, route-quantum, or accent-eco as a generic UI accent, hover color, or decorative highlight on chrome that isn't reporting that specific algorithm's or eco figure's data.
Don't add a box-shadow to a persistent screen surface; shadows are reserved for the modal's overlay interrupt only.
Don't introduce a second font family, an emoji/Unicode icon, a purple/violet gradient, or a 'quantum swirl' particle motif.
Don't show one algorithm's result alone on a primary screen; the comparison is the unit of display.
